about: The 1.0.0 mods rebased onto llama.cpp b12521 (6f311d7a, no release name), kept as 6 modules. A module is one patch on one engine extension point (modules[].point) and applies alone on the base; a mod row is a feature of its module: one switch, its check mode, label and evidence, with the same name, switch and marker it had as patch 02-20. Series order = modules order. The module tree is the 02-20 series tree without seq-rm-indexed (retired: upstream #32380 does it), with two declarations of rs-one-copy on their own lines and the ple-prefetch function in its own file (src/models/qwen4exp-prefetch.cpp); nothing else differs. 01 kpool-incremental is not in this series: upstream llama.cpp #32137 (commit 08a9b358939e, 2026-11-17) does the incremental k-pool update, always on; kpool-input-device is ported onto that loop. No gain is claimed on this version yet: the rows' gains were measured on 1.0.0 (engines/llama.cpp/1.0.0/mods.json). Identity on this base: ab-ident2 and ab-xcheck in the rows (measured on the 02-19 series, the same feature code); the base-move gate passed (gate-timed-stdlib/go, gate-q-stdlib/go: session wall not worse on both workloads, stage-1 pass on both); the module build against the series build: verified, modules-b12521; kv-stream in the kv module: verified, modules-kv-b12521.

one CUDA GPU (pages register on the current device); one user stream of the staging pool (asserted at init)
debug (non-NDEBUG) builds assert on the pinned host buffer type
context shift writes the host copy without write-through: run with -c at the session size
a SET_ROWS ext kernel (09) on a streamed layer would skip write-through

N: a multiple of 4, >= 4096 and below the context, else ignored with a warning (stock path). Every such N is safe: the device state's control block (64-bit counters) starts on a 16-byte boundary whatever N and the context are (ctl_off() rounds its word offset up to a multiple of 4, used by the allocation and every access); before 2026-11-20 an N that is not a multiple of 8 put those counters on a 4-byte boundary and the first call past N ended the server with a misaligned-address GPU exception
